classification.difficultyReason: Identify the exposed straight sides and arcs, using equality marks and an inferred central angle in part b.

content.prompt: Find the perimeter of these shapes. Answer to 1 d.p.

spec.description: Rectangle topped by a 45-degree sector centred at its upper-right corner. Preserve the dashed internal radius, paired vertical-side ticks and matching single ticks on the base and sloping radius.
spec.mathematics: Rectangle width and sector radius 6 cm; both vertical sides 7 cm; sector angle 45 degrees.
spec.answerVisibility: No perimeter answer or calculated arc length is visible.

answer.worked:
The single ticks show that the sector radius is $6\text{ cm}$.
$$\begin{align*}l&=\frac{45}{360}\times2\pi\times6\\P&=6+7+7+6+\frac{45}{360}\times2\pi\times6\\P&=26+\frac{3\pi}{2}\\P&\approx30.7\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Two equal solid sides form a pointed top above the remaining major circular arc. Two dashed radii meet at the circle centre. All four segments have matching single ticks, and the 45-degree angle remains at the apex.
spec.mathematics: The four equal segments form a rhombus with side 12 mm. Its opposite angle at the circle centre is 45 degrees, so the perimeter arc subtends 315 degrees.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied 12 mm and apex angle are visible; inferred angles and perimeter remain in the answer.

answer.worked:
The four equal sides form a rhombus, so the opposite angle at the circle centre is $45^\circ$. The radius is $12\text{ mm}$.
$$\begin{align*}\theta&=360^\circ-45^\circ=315^\circ\\l&=\frac{315}{360}\times2\pi\times12\\P&=12+12+\frac{315}{360}\times2\pi\times12\\P&=24+21\pi\\P&\approx90.0\text{ mm}\end{align*}$$
